title: House floor vote on H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act — data centers pay the full cost of grid upgrades
source: NEWS: the bill is on the House suspension calendar for the week of 2026-09-14 — docs.house.gov/floor (fetched direct 2026-09-15) lists 'H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act, as amended (Sponsored by Rep. Evans (CO) / Energy and Commerce Committee)' under items that may be considered under suspension of the rules, 'Added 09/10/2026 at 08:30 PM', and majorityleader.gov's weekly schedule (fetched direct 2026-09-15) places it in the Tuesday-Thursday block (09-15 to 09-17), House convening 10:00 Tue and 9:00 Wed/Thu with final votes expected by 3:00 pm. THE DAY IS DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED: no fetched source names which of the three days the vote lands on, so this entry takes the LAST scheduled legislative day of the calendared week. As of the Clerk's own record (clerk.house.gov/Votes/MemberVotes, CongressNum=119 Session=2nd, fetched 2026-09-15) the most recent roll call is No. 297 at 2026-09-14 19:16 and H.R. 9340 is not among the votes taken, so the vote was still pending at that timestamp. congress.gov and thehill.com both returned 403 on direct fetch and are not relied on. Stays estimate on three counts: the day is derived rather than read off a schedule, this calendar has no confirmed source prefix for a House floor calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: Proposed by the midterm-elections-2026-11-03 pulse of 2026-09-15 as the first DATED federal checkpoint on that ledger's leg 6 — the AI data-center backlash, which it argues is the real transmission channel from the midterms to this book. The bill (Evans R-CO / Castor D-FL, both in competitive races; Senate companion from Sen. Husted R-OH) cleared Energy & Commerce 52-0 in July 2026 and would require state utility regulators to CONSIDER adopting a federal standard making data centers pay the full cost of new generation and transmission built to serve them. Filed `low` deliberately and against the parent ledger's `high` tier: the operative requirement is a state-PUC 'shall consider', there is no appropriation and no direct cash-flow effect on any tracked name, and the parent pulse MEASURED the tape rather than assuming it — the equal-weight CEG/NRG/TLN/VST IPP basket carried -8.94pp of beta-adjusted excess drawdown over 09-04 to 09-15, which is only about -1.2 sigma against that basket's own daily excess sd of 2.60pp, so no policy attribution survives. Two things make the date worth tracking anyway: it is a 2/3 suspension vote (a real threshold, and E&E reported the data-center lobby grumbling about the reworked text), and it is the last House legislative week before members leave to campaign, so a miss here means no federal floor record on the issue before 11-03. Registered as FT-midterm-elections-2026-11-03-2, score-by 2026-09-18. If a Republican Cloakroom daily-floor page or a Clerk roll call later names the actual vote day, re-date this entry to it rather than defending 09-17; if the bill is pulled and never reaches the floor, the entry should be retired unfired rather than rolled forward.
